lines: Jordan Lee
+1 (555) 010-2468 | jordan.lee@example.com | example.com/code/jordan-lee
Date of birth: 14 Mar 1999 | Nationality: Canadian
EDUCATION
Western State University | M.S. in Computer Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Eastern Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, Country | Sep 2018 - Jun 2022
EXPERIENCE
Mobility Systems Company | Machine Learning Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Oct 2024 - May 2025
- Improved diagnostic accuracy by 35% after fine-tuning a domain adapter on validated tool-use trajectories with assistant-only loss masking.
- Designed a routing layer that limits each of 3 specialist agents and an independent reviewer to their in-scope signals, cutting reviewer disagreement with specialist findings from 14% to 6%.

- Trained the triage agent with GRPO on grouped tool-use rollouts and a reward that penalises redundant calls, cutting tool calls per case 18% and end-to-end latency 5% versus the SFT baseline at equal accuracy.
- Wrote the evaluation harness the team used to compare 14 adapter checkpoints on accuracy, citation quality and latency, catching 2 accuracy regressions before release.
- Fine-tuned the adapter with assistant-only loss masking so the model would learn to reproduce the tool outputs more faithfully.

- Built a diagnostics triage branch for an industrial inspection system that screens 800+ sensor signals per case with ML-extracted features, cutting the pending-case backlog 68% in the eight weeks after launch.
Eastern Robotics Co. | Junior Software Engineer | Metro City, Country | May 2023 - Jul 2024
- Cut GPU memory for fine-tuning the perception models by 4x by switching from FP32 to BF16 mixed precision.
- Reduced p95 API latency from 420 ms to 180 ms by adding a request cache and batching sensor reads, with load tests that fail the build if p95 exceeds 200 ms.
- Maintained the CI pipeline for the perception team's model releases and adds automated regression checks that shortened release cycles to 3 days.
- Migrated 30 robot-fleet services from cron jobs to an event queue with retries and dead-letter handling, removing the nightly backlogs that delayed morning dispatch.
PROJECTS
Agent Runtime Suite | Owner | TypeScript, Multi-Agent Systems | Aug 2025 - Present
- Drove adoption of AI-first engineering practices across the platform, accelerating delivery and improving outcomes for downstream teams.
- Kept working context under 10K tokens across a 100-turn stress test while the raw conversation grew 100x, using budgeted context layers and staged compaction.
- Separated concurrency pools and gated cache writes on stream completion, removing nested-pool deadlocks and lost tool results under 50-way fan-out.
Research-Agent Evaluation Framework | Contributor | LLM Evaluation | Feb 2025 - Jul 2025
- Integrated 8 citation and faithfulness metrics into an open-source research-agent framework's evaluation module.
- Showed the evaluator tracks injected degradation with a Kendall correlation of 0.89 across 400+ report-level trials that removed citations, sources and claims.
- Cut the pending-case backlog by two-thirds with a triage branch that screens 800+ sensor signals per case using ML-extracted features.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, TypeScript, Git
ML & Agents: PyTorch, LoRA, GRPO, agent evaluation

items.says: Make the contact link lead directly to current work you want employers to inspect.
items.because: It may otherwise lead to a general or outdated page.

items.says: Remove the date of birth and nationality.
items.because: They generally are not needed on a US résumé and take space from job-relevant information.

items.says: Confirm that “Expected Jun 2026” is still accurate.
Specify whether the 35% accuracy improvement is relative or a percentage-point change.
items.because: The headline result needs to be interpretable.

items.says: Identify the comparison behind the 35% improvement.
items.because: That makes the headline result credible and interpretable.

items.says: Clarify what “reviewer disagreement” measures and how it was assessed.
items.because: The reader needs to know why disagreement is the right outcome.

items.says: Check that the 18% and 5% reductions came from the same evaluation conditions.
Simplify method detail that is not important to the roles you are targeting.
If space is tight, prioritize the regressions caught over the checkpoint count.
items.because: The regressions are the clearer consequence of the work.

items.says: This bullet duplicates the first internship bullet.
Assistant-only loss masking does not, by itself, explain learning to reproduce tool outputs more faithfully.
Clarify how the triage branch contributed to the backlog reduction if other changes occurred during those eight weeks.
items.because: The branch’s contribution to the reduction is not clear.

items.says: Verify the measured 4× reduction in fine-tuning memory and account for any other changes.
items.because: Changing FP32 values to BF16 alone suggests a 2× reduction for those values, not necessarily a 4× reduction in total memory.

items.says: Clarify that the 200 ms threshold is a load-test check you implemented.
items.because: The wording should not imply that all production traffic stays below 200 ms.

items.says: Fix the tense inconsistency between “Maintained” and “adds”.
Clarify whether the regression checks caused the three-day release cycle.
items.because: CI maintenance generally may not have caused it.

items.says: Qualify the claim that nightly backlogs were removed if they were not eliminated consistently.
items.because: The outcome should match the evidence.

items.says: Remove the adoption-and-outcomes claim unless you can substantiate it.
items.because: It is much less specific than the two technical bullets beneath it.

items.says: Define what the “100x” growth compares against.
items.because: Otherwise the numbers are difficult to interpret.

items.says: Explain what the 100-turn stress test represents.
items.because: Otherwise the numbers are difficult to interpret.

items.says: Confirm that the deadlocks and lost results occurred before the changes and were absent in the 50-way test afterward.
items.because: That distinction supports the causal claim.

items.says: Identify your contribution boundary if the evaluation module was shared.
State what the Kendall correlation ranks.
items.because: That lets a reader judge what 0.89 demonstrates.

items.says: If important, explain how the trials were constructed.
items.because: That lets a reader judge what 0.89 demonstrates.

items.says: This bullet duplicates the internship backlog result.
The internship result appears under an unrelated project.
items.because: That could create doubt about where the work happened.

items.says: Git is listed as a programming language, but it is a tool.
Keep only skills you can discuss in depth.
